openai.sample_unit: patients (352 included in the primary propensity score–matched comparison)
models_evaluated: National Early Warning Score (NEWS)-based automated sepsis alert system

links.effect: Second versus first 6 months postimplementation: mortality 15.3% versus 25.0% (HR, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.36–0.86; P=0.017); blood cultures 58.5% versus 45.5% (P=0.019). Other bundle-component compliance was similar; neither period lacked the protocol.
links.quote: In total, 44 of 176 patients (25.0%) in the preliminary group and 27 of 176 patients (15.3%) in the SRP group died within 30 days of sepsis detection, revealing a significant difference in 30-day mortality between the two groups (HR, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.36–0.86; P=0.017) ( Figure 4 ).

links.effect: The SRP group had a lower 30-day mortality risk (hazard ratio, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.36-0.86; P=0.017) than the preliminary group.
